properties.value: SHA-family providers in the dependency tree: js-sha3@0.8.0 (via typechain and @ethersproject/keccak256), hash.js@1.1.7 (via elliptic), @noble/hashes (direct dep of hardhat-keystore, also via ethers v6), plus keccak@3.0.4 (via eip55). Declaration-level inventory; the repo's own SHA-256 operations are the hardhat-utils ethereum-cryptography wrapper (compiler checksum verification) and the keystore's HMAC-SHA-256, both filed separately.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: MD5 is available only through crypto-js@4.2.0, a transitive dependency of @ledgerhq/evm-tools (hardware-wallet tooling in the dev tree). No MD5 call exists anywhere in Hardhat source. Recorded as library-presence inventory, not as a used algorithm.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: All 44 sites are ===/!==/typeof checks on public blockchain identifiers — tx/block/event hashes and signature-field guards — across chai matchers, ignition-core, hardhat trace/verify code and network-helpers tests; most are null/undefined guards, none compares secret material. The one genuinely timing-sensitive comparison in this repo (keystore HMAC verification, hardhat-keystore encryption.ts:655) is NOT part of this object and is filed as its own finding. properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardhat's secp256k1 surface: hardhat-ethers installs EDR's Rust-native secp256k1 public-key derivation over ethers' JS implementation (installNativeSecp256k1 in initialization.ts, with self-check and JS fallback in native-secp256k1.ts); the hardhat core re-exports secp256k1PublicKeyFromSecretKey from EDR. The self-check vector at native-secp256k1.ts:17 is the well-known published Hardhat/Anvil account #0 private key — a public test key holding no funds. secp256k1 (ECDSA/ECDLP) is Shor-vulnerable

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: The lockfile entries are bcrypt-pbkdf@1.0.2 (the OpenSSH private-key KDF bridging bcrypt and PBKDF2), a transitive dependency of sshpk in the verdaccio local-registry chain, alongside bcryptjs@2.4.3 (used by verdaccio's htpasswd auth for the e2e test registry). No bcrypt-family call exists in Hardhat source; these are dev-tooling dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA presence in the dependency tree via ecdsa-sig-formatter@1.0.11 (dep of jwa, in the jws/jsonwebtoken chain pulled by @verdaccio/signature for local-registry JWTs) and via elliptic@6.6.1 (@ethersproject/signing-key, ethers v5 chain from @ledgerhw tooling). Hardhat source itself performs no ECDSA call — transaction signing happens inside ethers v6/EDR. Shor-vulnerable class; migration target ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 available via tweetnacl@0.14.5 (sshpk/bcrypt-pbkdf chain) and @noble/curves (ethers v6 chain); no Ed25519 signature operation anywhere in Hardhat source. Presence-only entry; Ed25519 is Shor-vulnerable (migration: ML-DSA-65).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH available via @noble/curves (transitive via ethers v6); Hardhat performs no ECDH key agreement anywhere — no standalone DH, no Signal-style protocol. Presence-only entry; ECDH is Shor-vulnerable (migration: ML-KEM-768).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 available via tweetnacl@0.14.5 and @noble/curves in the dependency tree; no X25519 exchange in Hardhat source. Presence-only entry; X25519 is Shor-vulnerable (migration: ML-KEM-768 / hybrid X25519+ML-KEM-768).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ethereum Keccak-256 (pre-SHA-3 padding) is the repo's dominant hash: chai matchers compute expected event-arg hashes (asserts.ts), hardhat-ethers registers EDR's native keccak256 into ethers (native-keccak256.ts, initialization.ts), hardhat-utils wraps ethereum-cryptography/keccak (crypto.ts:15-21), and hardhat re-exports EDR's keccak256 (edr/exports.ts:2). properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES available via @noble/ciphers (direct dependency of hardhat-keystore, and transitive via ethers v6) and crypto-js (via @ledgerhq). The keystore's live use is the AES-GCM-SIV variant (gcmsiv), filed separately with its call site. AES itself is quantum-resistant at 256-bit keys (Grover only); this entry records library availability.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-256 declared via @noble/hashes, a direct dependency of hardhat-keystore. It is genuinely used: the keystore's integrity MAC is HMAC-SHA-256 (hmac(sha256, hmacKey, json) at encryption.ts:631, filed as its own finding). The hardhat-utils ethereum-cryptography sha256 wrapper (compiler checksum verification) is filed separately as well.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: BLAKE3 available via @noble/hashes (direct dependency of hardhat-keystore); no BLAKE3 use found anywhere in the repo. Presence-only inventory entry — the library ships the algorithm whether or not this application calls it.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: SHA-3 available via @noble/hashes (direct dependency of hardhat-keystore); the keystore does not use SHA-3. The repo's pervasive Keccak-256 usage (Ethereum's pre-SHA-3-padding variant, via ethers/EDR/ethereum-cryptography) is covered by the separate SHA-3/keccak object ALG-052c24b2.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: AES-GCM declared via @noble/ciphers. The keystore's live use is the misuse-resistant GCM-SIV variant — gcmsiv(key, iv).encrypt() at encryption.ts:252 — which is filed as its own finding with the use site. 256-bit keys, 12-byte random IVs, IV-collision tolerance documented in the code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ChaCha20-Poly1305 available via @noble/ciphers (direct dependency of hardhat-keystore); the keystore does not use it — it uses AES-GCM-SIV. Presence-only entry; the shipped library provides the algorithm regardless of application calls.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: XSalsa20-Poly1305 provided by tweetnacl@0.14.5 (its secretbox construction), present transitively via bcrypt-pbkdf/sshpk in the verdaccio local-registry chain; no use in Hardhat source. Presence-only dev-tooling dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@0.14.5 in the dependency tree via bcrypt-pbkdf and sshpk (verdaccio local-registry chain for e2e publish tests). It exposes Ed25519, X25519 and XSalsa20-Poly1305 — each Shor/quantum-relevant when used, but none is called from Hardhat source. Dev-tooling dependency inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/hashes is a direct dependency of hardhat-keystore and supplies its entire hash/KDF layer: scrypt (master-key KDF, N=2^17/r=8/p=1), sha2 (HMAC-SHA-256 integrity MAC) and randomBytes (CSPRNG for 12-byte IVs and 32-byte salts). Also transitive via ethers v6. This is the keystore's primary crypto provider.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/ciphers is a direct dependency of hardhat-keystore and supplies AES-GCM-SIV (gcmsiv), which encrypts every secret stored in the keystore, including the wrapped data-encryption key and the wrapped HMAC key. Also transitive via ethers v6.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWT signing is performed only by jsonwebtoken@9.0.3 (default HS256) inside @verdaccio/signature, for the local npm registry used in e2e publish tests. Not a Hardhat runtime capability; dev tooling.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWS via jws@4.0.1/jwa@2.0.1 in the same @verdaccio/signature chain — local-registry auth tokens for e2e publish tests. Dev tooling only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: JWA algorithm identifiers (HS256 et al.) via jwa@2.0.1 in the verdaccio chain — used to sign the local registry's tokens during e2e tests. Dev tooling only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 is a transitive dependency of @ledgerhq/evm-tools (hardware-wallet tooling in the dev tree). It is a legacy browser-crypto library exposing MD5, SHA-1, SHA-2, AES, DES, etc. No crypto-js call exists in Hardhat source; presence is dev-dependency inventory only.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jwa@2.0.1 (JWA algorithm layer: HMAC, RSASSA, ECDSA, PBKDF2) via jws → jsonwebtoken → @verdaccio/signature. It exists only to support the local verdaccio npm registry used in e2e publish tests; not shipped in any Hardhat package.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jsonwebtoken@9.0.3 via @verdaccio/signature: signs/verifies the local registry's JWT auth tokens (default HS256) during e2e publish tests. Dev tooling only; not shipped. JWT/JWS asymmetry here is quantum-relevant only insofar as RSASSA/ECDSA modes would be used by verdaccio's configuration — outside this tree.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcryptjs@2.4.3 via verdaccio's htpasswd auth plugin, hashing the "test" user password for the local e2e registry (matching the htpasswd seeding in scripts/verdaccio/start.ts). Dev tooling only; no Hardhat source use.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: jws@4.0.1 via jsonwebtoken → @verdaccio/signature: JWS serialization for the local registry's auth tokens. Dev tooling for e2e publish tests; not shipped in Hardhat packages.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: elliptic@6.6.1 via @ethersproject/signing-key@5.8.0 — the ethers v5 chain pulled in by @ledgerhq hardware-wallet tooling. It implements JS secp256k1 ECDSA (Shor-vulnerable; migration ML-DSA-65). Hardhat source never calls it: the shipped path is ethers v6 plus EDR's native secp256k1. Presence-only dependency inventory.

properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 via elliptic (@ethersproject/signing-key, ethers v5 chain): provides SHA-1/SHA-2 implementations used inside elliptic's ECDSA. No direct use in Hardhat source.
